name: De Vinne Condensed 8pt 1900
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office and American Type Founders; the collective ATF page credits Central Type Foundry, St. Louis, for the design
description: 8-point De Vinne Condensed with flared serifs, a descending Q tail, double-storey a and g, and complete observed alphabets and figures.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, plus period, comma, dollar, double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus, and opening/closing double quotation marks. Space has a modern layout advance. The observed straight R remains available through ss01. No unsupported aliases or invented companions. Observed stacked fractions: ¼, ½, ¾, ⅓, ⅔, ⅛, ⅜, ⅝. Seven-eighths remains unencoded because both older impressions have a broken numerator and the later comparison is soft.
observed: The census specimen shows both complete 8-point alphabets and all ten figures. Matching ATF impressions supply clearer letters and figures. Eleven retained native pages document repeated samples and source-quality comparisons. The matching eight- and ten-point Poster De Vinne Condensed samples in the 1897 Handy Book, printed page 341, supply observed punctuation at the corresponding size. Whole stacked fractions come from the matching Handy Book poster (printed page 341) and fraction chart (printed page 40). The 1898 Desk Book and 1906 American Line fraction pages are retained as quality comparisons.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform scaling within each physical source, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. Named alternatives preserve observed R constructions. No independent width stretching or cross-size substitution.

revival.notes: Complete observed alphabets and figures, poster punctuation, 8 stacked fractions and a named straight R through ss01. Eleven native pages document the sources. Exact four-times derivatives, uniform source scales and measured row rotations are reproducible; the chart fractions use one scale fitted to seven matching whole fractions. No visible form is drawn or borrowed from another size. See source/METHOD.md.
